# Authlane documentation

> Authlane is the connection and tool control plane for SaaS applications.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://authlane.io/docs): Use Authlane as the connection and tool control plane for your SaaS application.
- [Quickstart](https://authlane.io/docs/quickstart): Connect a signed-in user and give their connected tools to an AI runtime.
- [How Authlane works](https://authlane.io/docs/concepts/how-authlane-works): Trace connection setup and local tool execution across the Authlane control-plane boundary.
- [Core concepts](https://authlane.io/docs/concepts/core-concepts): Understand Authlane resources and the tenant boundaries that relate them.
- [List available services](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/list-services): Load the tenant-enabled service catalog and render a useful empty state.
- [Connect a user](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/connect-user): Create, render, expire, and safely retry an origin-bound hosted connect session.
- [Connection lifecycle and status](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/connection-lifecycle): Interpret connection states and recover through refresh, reconnect, and disconnect flows.
- [Load user-scoped tools](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/user-tools): Bind an authenticated external user, select an adapter, and run provider tools locally.
- [Receive lifecycle webhooks](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/webhooks): Verify signed connection lifecycle events and process retries idempotently.
- [Production hardening](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/production-hardening): Protect authenticated AI routes with bounded input, exact origins, rate limits, and redacted logs.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/typescript): Use the server-only TypeScript SDK for catalog, connection, capability, and tool workflows.
- [React connect UI](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/react): Embed the hosted Authlane connect UI with a short-lived origin-bound URL.
- [Python SDK](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/python): Use Authlane from Python with typed Result handling and user-scoped local tools.
- [Vercel AI SDK](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/vercel-ai): Build Vercel AI tools for one authenticated Authlane user and stream a model response.
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/openai-agents): Run an OpenAI agent with tools bound to one authenticated Authlane user.
- [Mastra](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/mastra): Create a Mastra agent with Authlane tools scoped to the signed-in SaaS user.
- [Agno](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/agno): Run an Agno agent with Authlane tools bound to one authenticated external user.
- [LangChain](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/langchain): Build a LangChain agent with Authlane tools scoped to one authenticated SaaS user.
- [Local MCP server](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/local-mcp): Connect a caller-owned MCP transport to one authenticated user’s Authlane tools.
- [Framework adapters](https://authlane.io/docs/sdk/frameworks): Choose a shipped adapter after binding one authenticated external user.
- [Authentication](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/authentication): Scoped SaaS keys and short-lived browser sessions
- [Errors and rate limits](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/errors-and-rate-limits): Handle Authlane error envelopes, retry headers, idempotency, and safe backoff.
- [List services](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/services/list-services): Return services enabled for the authenticated tenant
- [List connection statuses](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/connections/list-connections): Return an effective connection status for every enabled tenant service
- [Get capabilities](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/connections/capabilities): Return statuses and MCP/OpenAI definitions in one hot-read snapshot
- [Create connect session](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/connections/create-connect-session): Create a short-lived browser handoff bound to one user, service allowlist, and exact HTTPS origin
- [Issue a credential lease](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/connections/create-credential-lease): Issue audited access-only credential material to a trusted server-side caller
- [Authorize a service](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/oauth/authorize): Start PKCE OAuth from a valid connect session in the hosted connect UI
- [OAuth callback](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/oauth/callback): Validate OAuth state and PKCE, store encrypted credentials, and return to the hosted connect UI
- [List tools](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/tools/list-tools): Return MCP tools or OpenAI functions for currently usable connections
- [API overview](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference/introduction): Use the scoped Authlane control-plane API and open the complete read-only OpenAPI reference.
- [API reference](https://authlane.io/docs/api-reference): Inspect the complete read-only Authlane OpenAPI control-plane contract.
- [GitHub](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/github): Use the local GitHub adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Linear](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/linear): Use the local Linear adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Jira](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/jira): Use the local Jira adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Sentry](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/sentry): Use the local Sentry adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Slack](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/slack): Use the local Slack adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Discord](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/discord): Use the local Discord adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Gmail](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/gmail): Use the local Gmail adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Notion](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/notion): Use the local Notion adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Google Drive](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/google-drive): Use the local Google Drive adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Google Calendar](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/google-calendar): Use the local Google Calendar adapter with Authlane credentials
- [HubSpot](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/hubspot): Use the local HubSpot adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Salesforce](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/salesforce): Use the local Salesforce adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Pipedrive](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/pipedrive): Use the local Pipedrive adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Stripe](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/stripe): Use the local Stripe adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Airtable](https://authlane.io/docs/integrations/airtable): Use the local Airtable adapter with Authlane credentials
- [Build a connection](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/custom-integrations): Add canonical definitions and a direct-execution adapter for an Authlane service.
- [Integration contract](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/integration-contract): Define a canonical service contract and matching direct-execution adapters without gateway behavior.
- [Local integration testing](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/integration-testing): Verify integration contracts, OAuth boundaries, redaction, tenant isolation, and direct provider execution.
- [Self-hosting](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/self-hosting): Run Authlane as one hardened application with PostgreSQL and Redis.
- [Provider OAuth configuration](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/oauth-setup): Configure provider applications for Authlane hosted authorization and callbacks.
- [Security model](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/security): Apply Authlane tenant, browser, credential, OAuth, and provider-execution boundaries.
- [Key rotation and security operations](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/security-operations): Launch, rotate keyrings, restore safely, and respond to Authlane security incidents.
- [Performance](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/performance): Benchmark and operate the cached capabilities hot-read path against the 100 ms P95 target.
- [Troubleshooting](https://authlane.io/docs/guides/troubleshooting): Diagnose Authlane SDK tuple errors across identity, OAuth, leases, cache, and webhooks.
- [Authlane agent marketplace](https://authlane.io/docs/ai-tools/marketplace): Install the repository-owned Authlane plugin and choose one of its two shipped skills.
- [Claude Code plugin](https://authlane.io/docs/ai-tools/claude): Install, verify, update, and remove the repository-owned Authlane plugin in Claude Code.
- [Codex plugin](https://authlane.io/docs/ai-tools/codex): Install, verify, refresh, and remove the repository-owned Authlane plugin in Codex.
- [Cursor plugin](https://authlane.io/docs/ai-tools/cursor): Install, verify, update, and remove the repository-owned Authlane plugin in Cursor.
